title: In This Town, Never Let Go on the Ice

lines.text: In this town, something skates under the frozen lake, upside down, copying everything you do.
So you never let go of your partner's hand.
We call it the Underskater.
It can only copy one skater at a time.
Hold hands, and it can't choose.
But let go out on the ice, and it picks whoever is alone.
And the one who walks off the lake isn't always the one who skated on.
So every pair on the lake holds hands. Always.
Mrs. Dunn calls her son off the ice the second his friend lets go.
And someone scratched two words into the ice by the shore.
Never alone.
Leo was my best friend.
We skated every evening after school.
And Leo always wanted to race.
That night, he yanked his hand out of mine.
Catch me!
He laughed, all alone in the middle of the lake.
And under the ice, the shadow stopped copying me.
It turned toward Leo.
I skated as hard as I could.
Under him, it lined up with his blades. Perfectly.
I grabbed his hand.
There was a crack. A flash of white.
And Leo was still holding my hand.
We walked off the ice together.
He didn't say a word.
And his hand was freezing.
He didn't let go, not even on the shore.
I looked back at the lake.
Under the ice, Leo was pounding on it from below.
Screaming, without a sound.
The Leo next to me smiled.
I grabbed his hand a second too late.
Leo walked me home that night.
The real one is still under the ice.
